summary.whatChanges: `StreamingApi.abort()` now wraps each abort subscriber call in a try/catch and swallows rejected promises returned by listeners, so a throwing or async-rejecting listener no longer stops remaining listeners from running or produces an unhandled rejection. Tests cover sync throws, rejecting thenables, and async listeners.
behaviorChanges: A listener registered via onAbort() that throws synchronously no longer propagates the error out of abort(); subsequent listeners still run.
Listeners returning a rejected promise or rejecting thenable no longer trigger unhandled rejection events.
abort() still sets aborted = true and invokes all subscribers regardless of individual listener failures.
risks: Listener errors are silently swallowed with no logging, making cleanup failures hard to diagnose.
Async listener completion is not awaited, so abort() returns before async cleanup finishes.
